newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up on selective buying.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up on selective buying.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended up on Tuesday on active buying mainly from overseas, brokers said.
The index rose 0.560 points or 1.08 percent to 52.269 points, on volume of 15.2 million shares worth $6.5 million. Of 41 B shares, 35 traded, with 17 up, seven flat and 11 down.
Brokers said cuts in interest rates last week encouraged overseas investors to buy selected stocks.

"Investors mainly focussed on stocks listed in 1996, on expectations of better results," one broker said. "Individual stocks will perform differently depending on their interim results to be posted in the coming days."
"The index will move around 52 points until all interim results are known by the end of August," a second broker said.

Tientsin Marine was the star on active trading, on expectations of good net profits because of its container business, brokers said. It rose $0.044 or 16.54 percent to $0.310, on volume of 2.9 million shares.
Shanghai Automation Instrumentation performed the worst after posting poor interim results, falling $0.010 or 5.49 percent to $0.172, on volume of 79,400 shares.
Shanghai A shares had a technical rebound after sharp losses in recent days but trading was not active because of cautious market sentiment, brokers said.
The A index rose 15.219 points or 1.88 percent to 822.689 points, on volume of 231.9 million shares worth 2.1 billion yuan. The SSE 30 index rose 45.359 points or 2.21 percent to 2098.880 points.
Tianjin Storage was the star, jumping 0.71 yuan or 9.69 percent to 8.03 yuan, on volume of 1.9 million shares.
